segments: The tenth dynasty:
The Arab kings.
twelve thousand camels,
and the rest fled.
And in the year 572
[5]72 of the Arabs,
Salah al-Din again encamped against Aleppo.
And when al-Salih saw that his force was not sufficient,
he acted with humility
and asked for peace.
And Salah al-Din consented,
and made a general peace with Aleppo, Mosul, and Little Armenia.
And when the peace was confirmed,
al-Salih sent out a young sister whom he had to Salah al-Din,
and she asked him for 'Azaz,
and he gave it to her.
And he left and went to Damascus,
and married the wife of Nur al-Din, who was called 'Ismat al-Din among women.
And he appointed his brother Shams al-Din Turanshah in Damascus,
and he himself returned to Egypt.
And he built for both cities, Egypt (Fustat) and Cairo, a single wall enclosing them,
and on the mountain in between he built a citadel.
And in the year 573,
573 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1489
1489 of the Greeks,
he encamped against Ascalon,
and pillaged and took captives,
and shed much Christian blood.
The Franks, moreover, were in great terror,
because in that youthful king of Jerusalem the disease of leprosy had begun.
Nevertheless, even so,
that sick king assembled the remnant of his forces,
and dismounted from his riding beast,
and fell upon his face before the Holy Cross, weeping.
And the hearts of all of them were moved with groaning,
and they swore {OCR?} that they would not turn their backs,
but would endure in the conflict unto death.
Therefore they waited until the Turks had penetrated into the country,
and became preoccupied with taking captives,
and neglected preparation for battle and became slack,
because they had become convinced of the weakness of the Franks.
Therefore the Franks mounted,
and came and overtook the Turks as they were crossing a certain river.
And the Lord stirred up a violent tempest,
which swept the sand from the side of the Franks onto the Turks.
And when they were blinded,
the sword of the Franks prevailed over them,
and they turned their backs,
and went astray in a trackless waste in those desolate deserts.
And for five days the Franks were pursuing them and finding them in bands and capturing and killing them;
and Salah al-Din, with a few men, escaped to Cairo.
